title: Dynamical phase transition for a logarithm observable in chaotic systems
abstract: We consider the full distribution $P_N(A)$ of the dynamical observable $A = - \sum_{i=1}^N \ln x_i$ where $x_1, \dots, x_N$ is a sequence generated by a chaotic map $f(x)$ via $x_{n+1} = f(x_n)$. We study the particular cases where $f(x)$ is the doubling, tent or logistic map, and focus on the limit $N \gg 1$. Typical fluctuations of $A$ are Gaussian with mean $\left\langle A\right\rangle$ and variance which are both of order $\sim N$. We find that the left tail of the distribution ($A < \left\langle A\right\rangle$) scales as $P_{N}(A) \sim e^{-NI(A/N)}$, and calculate the rate function $I(a)$ which depends on the map $f(x)$. Interestingly, we find that the right tail of the distribution ($A > \left\langle A\right\rangle$) follows an anomalous scaling: $P_{N}(A) \sim e^{-N^{1/3} F((A-\left\langle A\right\rangle) / N^{2/3})}$. The large-deviation function $F(y)$ has a universal form for the three maps, differing only in the scaling constants. At a critical value $y=y_c$, it exhibits a corner singularity which has the character of a condensation transition. The transition separates between a subcritical phase $0< y<y_c$ in which the fluctuations are Gaussian and arise homogeneously from all of the $x_i$'s, and a supercritical phase $y>y_c$ in which a small fraction of the $x_i$'s give a macroscopic contribution to the fluctuation. Despite this anomalous behavior of the right tail, we find that the cumulants of the distribution $P_N(A)$ grow linearly with $N$ at large $N$, and calculate the associated coefficients.
summary: This paper analyzes the statistical fluctuations of a logarithm observable in chaotic dynamical systems like the logistic map. It demonstrates that while typical fluctuations are Gaussian, the rare events (right tail) exhibit anomalous scaling. This anomaly signals a dynamical phase transition, separating a homogeneous regime from one dominated by a few 'big jumps' in the sequence.
main_problem: The paper investigates the large deviations and anomalous scaling of a dynamical observable, $A = -\sum \ln x_i$, generated by iterating a chaotic map.
main_result: It finds that while the left tail follows standard Large Deviation Principle scaling, the right tail exhibits anomalous scaling characterized by a corner singularity, indicating a dynamical phase transition.
method: The analysis employs Large Deviation Theory (LDP), calculating the rate function $I(a)$ via the Scaled Cumulant Generating Function (SCGF) and analyzing the transition using saddle-point approximations.
model_or_system: The system is defined by discrete-time, one-dimensional chaotic dynamics using well-known maps: the doubling, tent, or logistic map. The observable is the logarithm of the product of the sequence elements.
key_observables: The observable $A$, its mean $\langle A angle$, its variance $	ext{Var}(A)$, the rate function $I(a)$, and the anomalous scaling function $F(y)$.
important_parameters: The system size $N$ (in the limit $N \gg 1$), and the deviation parameter $y$ relative to the critical value $y_c$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the initial condition is drawn from the steady-state distribution and relies on approximations like the parabolic form of the rate function near the transition.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the theoretical rate function $I(a)$ with numerical results for the probability distribution $P_N(A)$ at increasing system sizes $N$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the typical Gaussian fluctuations and the standard LDP for the left tail. It then focuses on the anomalous right tail, deriving the scaling function $F(y)$ and identifying the critical point $y_c$ that marks the dynamical phase transition.
why_interesting: The study of anomalous scaling and dynamical phase transitions in chaotic systems provides theoretical tools applicable to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, which underpins many open quantum system dynamics.
